# `mileage-rate` commands

## `mileage-rate delete`

Remove the mileage rate that starts on a date; the earlier rate then holds until the next one. Reimbursements already written keep the rate they were paid at.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/mileage-rate.delete` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow mileage-rate delete 2027-01-01 --reason "Entered a year early" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "mileage-rate delete", "input": {"effective_date": "2027-01-01"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `effective_date` | `EFFECTIVE_DATE` | string | yes | no | — | minimum length 10; maximum length 10; pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$" |

## `mileage-rate set`

Set the mileage rate per mile from an effective date, as the anchor's Mileage Rates window does (the standard rate changes each January). A rate holds from its date until the next one. Setting a date that already has a rate replaces it. The rate in effect on a trip end date is the deduction rate on the mileage reports and the default rate of `trip reimburse`; it is never stored on the trip.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer-work |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/mileage-rate.set` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow mileage-rate set --effective-date 2026-01-01 --rate 0.70 --reason "Standard rate for 2026" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "mileage-rate set", "input": {"effective_date": "2026-01-01", "rate": "0.70"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `effective_date` | `--effective-date` | string | yes | no | — | First date the rate applies to; it holds until the next rate.; minimum length 10; maximum length 10; pattern "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$" |
| `rate` | `--rate` | string | yes | no | — | Deduction rate per mile in the home currency, such as 0.655; at most four decimal places.; minimum length 1; maximum length 16 |
